question: Does any ordered pair of the registered A-Z or KRYPTOS-deduplicated alphabet orders, forward or reversed and at any relative rotation, satisfy all 24 aligned crib equations for any of the 39 registered decimal-primer survivors?
model: c(C_i)-p(P_i)=k[i] modulo 26 at all 24 aligned cribs, with an ordered plaintext/ciphertext pair drawn from four registered alphabet orders and every relative rotation

domain.primers: the exact 39 sorted survivors in PRIMERS-0001 run-002
domain.global_symmetry: common rotation of both alphabets preserves index differences, so plaintext rotation zero and all relative ciphertext rotations are complete

evaluation_unit: individual crib equations; exactly 24 are evaluated for every candidate model
dependencies: Cargo.lock offline; Python standard library; no network or stochastic input
prior_observation: Before registration, an exploratory read-only Python probe evaluated only ciphertext rotation zero. It found no full match, a best score of 6/24, and histogram 0:264, 1:225, 2:87, 3:38, 4:6, 5:3, 6:1. It did not inspect rotations 1-25 and did not alter this complete domain.
falsification_criterion: Any survivor falsifies the scoped exclusion; any missing or duplicate canonical model, incorrect first-mismatch certificate, recurrence, trace, histogram, aggregate, regression hash, or Rust/Python disagreement fails the experiment.
limitations: A zero-survivor result excludes only the four registered explicit alphabet orders, their ordered pairs and relative rotations under this exact recurrence model.
No dictionary, other keyword alphabet, tableau convention, key offset, transposition, language score or inferred plaintext is tested.
A survivor would establish crib compatibility only, not plaintext recovery or historical attribution.
The Python implementation is an independently derived algorithm written by the same project coordinator, not a fresh-context external A7 review.
